story.title: YouTube adds new creator tools like video A/B testing, dynamic thumbnails, and live dubbing

facts.text: YouTube already allows creators to A/B test titles and thumbnails, and from 2027, this feature will let creators upload and test three different cuts for Shorts.

There’s also a Dynamic Thumbnails feature, with which creators can upload multiple thumbnails and leave it to YouTube to determine which thumbnail to show viewers that is most likely to spark their interest.
The platform is also giving creators new ways to go live.
Early next year, YouTube will pilot auto-dubbing on live videos to translate creators’ speech into other languages in real time.
The company is also launching a “live showdown” feature, which lets creators co-host streams together, and even get paired with other creators currently streaming through “live creator matchmaking.”
In a bid to help creators reach more people, YouTube on Wednesday unveiled a slew of new tools, many of which use AI to try out different tactics on videos to find what makes them perform best.

YouTube’s data also confirms what we know about the growth of the microdrama industry : In the first half of 2026, microdramas on YouTube surpassed 6.5 billion views, and their watch time rose 50% year-over-year.
YouTube also shared data that provides insight into how people are using the platform.
Creators can also apply these tools to their existing catalog.
If a creator allows it, Ask Studio will be able to autonomously monitor thumbnail performance and create tests to refine older videos.
Those tests can locate what YouTube calls “outlier videos”: exceptional performers that can inspire future uploads.
New Insights and Research data in YouTube Studio can add more context to those outliers, and the same philosophy is being applied to thumbnails, too.
After bringing dynamic insertion to its ads at last year’s Made On event, YouTube is now introducing dynamic thumbnails.
By automatically switching between multiple preview images, YouTube is aiming to maximize reach among specific audience segments.
If you’ve tuned into previous editions of YouTube’s product spiel, the headlines for the 2026 presentation may sound familiar.
Those experiments already allow creators to pit multiple titles and thumbnails against each other to determine which one performs better.
Soon, that process will expand to entire videos.
By A/B testing multiple cuts of the same clip, creators can identify the version that best resonates with their audience.
AI suggestions delivered by Google’s Gemini models are saving time for users while turning YouTube into a more targeted experience.
For social shoppers, an expanded Ask YouTube feature will turn questions and follow-ups into interactive product recommendations that show up across TV and mobile surfaces.
At Made On, Mohan officially announced the new Custom Feeds .
That tool can turn users’ suggestions into fully populated landing pages that cut across specific content categories.
When it comes to TikTok, however, YouTube is borrowing much more than just AI-powered updates.
It is leaning into the growing popularity of microdramas by expanding its Series feature .
TikTok has found ways to monetize serialized short-form collections , and YouTube is taking a step in that direction with the introduction of Shorts Series .
In other words, YouTube homepage shelves will now deliver the granular recommendations Netflix users have come to expect.
To make its own Vertical Live streams as functional as their TikTok analogues, YouTube is introducing several new broadcast options.
Go Live Together will enable co-hosting on those streams, Live showdowns will turn them into collaborative fundraisers, and Live auto-dubbing will bring streaming content to viewers across the globe.
If you think AI-powered personalization is already ubiquitous on YouTube, just wait.
Made On YouTube 2026 shows that Mohan and his deputies are paying attention to the formats, features, and products that are shining on other platforms.
A lot of that has to do with AI; YouTube, like Spotify, wants to automate audio recommendations, which is why it’s bringing Ask Music — its version of the Spotify DJ — to the YouTube Music app.
All of those Vertical Live updates are due to arrive in “early 2027.” From that point on, YouTube has no plans to slow down.
Instead, users can expect the flurry of new features to continue.
The $100 billion creator payout milestone represents approximately 45% of YouTube's total advertising revenue over the four-year period, according to industry estimates.
This revenue sharing rate significantly exceeds traditional media industry standards where content creators typically receive 10-15% of advertising revenue.
YouTube unveiled its largest creator features update at Made on YouTube 2025, introducing AI-powered content creation tools and marking $100 billion paid to creators over four years.
YouTube Partner Program membership reached 3 million channels, with 700,000 joining over the past three years.
Gross Merchandise Volume through YouTube Shopping grew 5X year-over-year with over 500,000 creators enrolled globally as of July 2025.
The integration of Veo 3 Fast represents significant computational requirements for YouTube's infrastructure.
According to technical documentation, the system processes text prompts through Google DeepMind's neural networks while maintaining 480p output resolution to balance quality with processing speed.
The reduced latency design enables real-time content generation on mobile devices, requiring substantial backend optimization.
The announcement represents significant developments for digital marketing strategies, particularly regarding creator partnerships and video advertising.
PPC Land has extensively covered YouTube's expanding role in the creator economy , noting the platform's evolution from simple video hosting to comprehensive business infrastructure.
Other features deploy across all YouTube markets with varying timelines.
This marks the first time creators can generate video content with sound from text prompts directly within the platform.
The feature launches initially in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand, with expansion planned for additional markets.
Creator economy growth impacts traditional advertising agency models as brands increasingly allocate budgets toward creator partnerships rather than conventional media placements.
PPC Land analysis shows creator content marketing receives 89% advertiser approval , with 44% of marketers planning investment increases.
Enhanced targeting capabilities in YouTube Shopping align with broader programmatic advertising trends.
TikTok's Effect House and Instagram's AR tools provide comparable creation features, but lack the integrated monetization infrastructure YouTube offers through its Partner Program.
The combination of AI content creation with established revenue sharing creates competitive advantages for creator retention and platform loyalty.
This tool converts dialogue from eligible videos into musical soundtracks for Shorts.
Creators can specify musical styles including chill, danceable, or fun vibes while maintaining attribution to original content creators.
Meta's Reels platform competes directly in short-form video content but relies primarily on external AI tools rather than integrated generation capabilities.
Live streaming received what YouTube describes as its largest update ever.
Over 30% of daily logged-in viewers watched live content in Q2 2025 according to platform statistics.
New features include simultaneous horizontal and vertical streaming with unified chat, practice mode for new streamers, and AI-powered highlight extraction for Shorts creation.
The dynamic brand segment insertion feature addresses advertiser demands for campaign flexibility that competing platforms struggle to match.
Traditional social media sponsorships require permanent content integration, while YouTube's system enables post-publication modifications and market-specific targeting.
Creators can ask questions like "catch me up on how my last video is performing" or "tell me what my community is saying about my editing style."
Auto-tagging capabilities will identify and tag eligible products mentioned in videos, reducing manual creator workload.
Music features focus on fan engagement through YouTube Music integration.
Traditional production barriers that favored established creators or brands with larger budgets may diminish as text-to-video generation becomes accessible.
Title A/B testing expanded to support three title and thumbnail combinations per video, building on the thumbnail testing feature used over 15 million times since 2023.
YouTube is giving creators more tools to test, optimize and distribute their content as the platform expands its use of artificial intelligence across video creation and discovery.
YouTube is expanding Ask Studio, its AI assistant for creators, to mobile apps.
More viewers are watching YouTube through household televisions, with more than half of the platform’s top 100 creators having the living room as their most-watched viewing interface.
For creators, the tools could reduce some of the manual work involved in optimising a channel.
YouTube is also extending some of these capabilities to older videos.
With a creator’s permission, Ask Studio can monitor thumbnail performance and automatically create tests to determine whether different thumbnails improve how viewers respond to existing content.
The tools are designed to help creators understand what works on their channels, improve existing videos and reach audiences in more markets.
YouTube already allows creators to test different titles and thumbnails to determine which versions perform better.
The company plans to expand this capability in 2027 by allowing creators to upload and test up to three different cuts of a Short.
The format gives YouTube another way to make live content more interactive while encouraging collaborations between creators.
As YouTube continues to expand beyond traditional video recommendations, the platform is positioning AI as a central part of how creators produce, optimise, distribute and monetise their work.

The company announced a series of new creator features on Wednesday, including AI-powered feedback through Ask Studio, video A/B testing, dynamic thumbnails, automated product tagging and real-time dubbing for live videos.
